question: What does the NBFC owe the borrower if it is late in handing back property documents after the loan is repaid?
reference: If documents are not released (or the charge not removed) within 30 days of full repayment and the delay is attributable to the NBFC, it must compensate the borrower at Rs 5,000 for each day of delay, and communicate the reasons for the delay.
answer:
According to para 39 of the Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025, if the delay in releasing original movable / immovable property documents beyond 30 days after full repayment/settlement is attributable to the NBFC, it must communicate the reasons for the delay and compensate the borrower at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay [1][2]. 

Under para 40 of the Directions, in the event of loss or damage to original documents, the NBFC must also assist the borrower in obtaining duplicate/certified copies and bear the associated costs in addition to the daily compensation, with the delayed period penalty calculated after an additional time of 30 days (i.e., after a total period of 60 days) [1][5]. 

Furthermore, as stated in para 41 of the Directions, this compensation is without prejudice to the borrower's rights to obtain any other compensation under applicable law [5].

question: When can an NPA loan account be upgraded back to standard?
reference: Only if the entire arrears of interest and principal are paid by the borrower.
answer: Under para 24 of the Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions, 2025, loan accounts classified as NPAs may be upgraded to ‘standard’ asset only if the entire arrears of interest and principal are paid by the borrower [1][2]. For borrowers having more than one credit facility, upgradation is permitted only upon the repayment of entire arrears of interest and principal pertaining to all credit facilities (para 25 of the Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions, 2025) [1][2]. For accounts classified as NPA or retained as NPA on restructuring, upgradation occurs only when all outstanding facilities perform satisfactorily during the 'specified period' by servicing principal and interest as per the terms of payment (para 191 of the Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025) [3]. In addition, project finance accounts downgraded to NPA due to DCCO non-compliance may be upgraded after satisfactory performance post actual DCCO under para 115, or upon successful implementation of a resolution plan provided no further deferment request for DCCO is received under para 116 of the Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025 [4][6].
